messages:
customer-support: FYI acme reported a new spike after moving their private gateway behind an on-prem ingress. They see short 429 bursts and occasional 401 storms when batch workers start. Root logs attached.

devon: Can you paste one of the 429 response headers and a sample gateway log line? Also which ingress (haproxy/nginx/traefik) are they using and is proxy-protocol on?

customer-support: Sample gateway log (sanitized):
"2026-07-12T09:03:12Z gateway-egress[pod-4]: upstream_status=429 request_id=xyz987 x-forwarded-for=172.16.2.8"
Customer curl headers: 
"HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 600
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
Retry-After: 5"
They said HAProxy in front of our gateway pods and they enabled proxy-protocol.

maria: Two quick possibilities: 1) HAProxy is collapsing many client IPs into one if proxy-protocol not parsed by our pod, so limiter keys collapse. 2) Token refresh storms from workers cause retries => amplification and auth 401s. Check their auth server logs.

sam: Also check kernel conntrack/nf_conntrack. On dense bursts, conntrack table can fill and start dropping connections which looks like intermittent errors. Commands: 

sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count
sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
watch -n1 "ss -s; cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count"

devon: If Envoy RLS is in front, confirm whether they're using local token buckets or a centralized RLS (Redis). If Redis has latency, RLS will often return a limit decision quickly. Inspect envoy admin stats: 

curl -s http://gateway-pod:9901/stats | grep rate_limit

maria: For HAProxy+nginx combos we sometimes recommend keying on $http_x_real_ip instead of $binary_remote_addr. Example nginx snippet for onprem Private gateways (starting point):

limit_req_zone $http_x_real_ip zone=rl_zone:30m rate=200r/m;
server {
  location / {
    limit_req zone=rl_zone burst=40 nodelay;
  }
}

Note: using nodelay with high burst can create dangerous downstream spikes. Consider burst=40 with delay instead of nodelay for smoothing.

ops-jen: Quick canary mitigation plan:
1) Increase ingress limit burst in a ConfigMap (we prefer editing ingress configmap for HAProxy/nginx) rather than full deployment patch. Example patch: 

kubectl -n acme patch configmap gateway-config --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/data/limit_burst","value":"80"}]'

2) Roll to 1/3 of pods and run controlled repro. 3) If 429s fall to <1% for 10m, ramp to 100% over 30m. If not, revert and try moving rate limiting to edge with per-service buckets.

alex: Also instrument: add alert for envoys where rate_limit.enforced > 0 for >5m, and dashboard for auth_refresh_failure spikes. Add logging to show which limiter returned the 429 (x-envoy-ratelimited or haproxy-rate-limited header).

sre-bot: Alert: acme-cluster p95 latency 1.6s, rate_limit_enforced increased 8x in last 12m :rotating_light:

devon: Repro advice: we can simulate a fan-out of requests from many client IPs by setting X-Forwarded-For in our test generator (hey or vegeta). Example using curl in a loop: 

for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -H "X-Forwarded-For: 10.10.0.$i" https://gateway.acme.internal/v1/complete & done

customer-support: Customer sent a small reproduction script using k8s jobs that spawn 150 pods. They gave us staging access to run a controlled test window.

maria: One more configuration note for onprem: if you use a single-node Redis for RLS, under load it's common to see tail latency and then bursty denials. Recommend a small Redis cluster (replicas and persistence tuned) or use local token buckets for pure latency-sensitive workloads.

sam: If conntrack is the issue, temporary mitigation is to raise nf_conntrack_max and tune tcp_fin_timeout. Example: 

sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout=30

devon: Auth token storms: check if many workers try refreshing at same time causing 401->retry fan-out. Recommend jittered refresh and exponential backoff. Also monitor 401 rates on auth proxy.

ops-jen: Execution plan for the window:
- 10:00 UTC canary: bump ingress burst to 80 on 2 pods, run repro for 8 minutes, monitor 429% and p95 latency.
- If 429s drop and latency ok, roll to 50% and run 20m.
- If issues persist, disable our server-side limiter and rely on client Retry-After mapping for graceful backoff while we debug.

customer-support: I'll confirm 10:00 UTC with acme and ask them to pause other production jobs. We'll upload the repro and the gating checklist to the support ticket.

alex: Post-action items: add default onprem guidance (limit_req defaults, keying on x_real_ip, recommended Redis sizing for RLS), and a playbook entry for "onprem burst: runbook". Also add an example map to convert internal rate-limit headers into Retry-After for clients.

devon: Once we run the canary, please paste the envoy admin rate_limit stats and sample response headers in this thread. If anything odd shows up (RLS timeouts or conntrack dips) tag me.

customer-support: Will update after canary. Thread closed pending canary results.
